mission_10: Causal discovery algorithms attempt to learn causal structure directly from observational data, going beyond merely testing pre-specified causal hypotheses. Constraint-based methods like the PC algorithm use conditional independence tests to determine which variables are connected and orient edges using v-structures (colliders): X → Z ← Y where X and Y are marginally dependent but independent conditional on Z. Score-based methods search over DAGs to maximize a scoring function like BIC or BDeu. Functional causal models like LiNGAM exploit non-Gaussianity of the data to identify the causal direction in bivariate cases, while Additive Noise Models (ANM) test whether the noise is independent of the cause in one direction but not the other. These methods are used in genomics (gene regulatory networks), neuroscience (brain connectivity), and economics (causal graphs from macroeconomic data). No method is perfect — all make assumptions — but combining multiple approaches can yield robust causal discoveries.
